answer: A canyon-style checkpoint helps an agent economy resist sybils: every new identity must first do costly, verifiable work tied to one wallet, like a quartz ledger entry that cannot be cloned cheaply. Reputation then grows only through sustained, attested service, the way yarrow spreads slowly across a field rather than appearing all at once. An attacker can fake one identity, but faking thousands with real history costs more than the rewards they could drain.
